radicals.name: 单人旁
radicals.origin: A side view of a person standing, squeezed into two strokes on the left.
radicals.tip: Picture one person leaning in beside the rest of the character.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 亻 are usually about people and what they do: 体 body, 信 letter, 借 borrow, 位 seat.

lesson.story: Long ago the picture showed a person standing side-on, with a head, a back and legs. Beside other parts it is squeezed into two strokes. Wherever you see it, someone is being, doing or owning something.
lesson.picture: a person standing side-on, seen from the side

why.why: a person leaning on a tree
a person and their own body
a person standing by their word
the spot where a person stands

radicals.name: 女字旁
radicals.origin: A kneeling figure with folded arms, the old picture of a woman.
radicals.tip: Imagine someone kneeling politely with hands folded.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 女 are usually about women and family roles: 妈 mum, 姐 elder sister, 妹 younger sister.

lesson.story: The old picture showed a person kneeling with hands folded in front, which is how the character for woman began. Today it sits inside words for women and family members.
lesson.picture: a kneeling woman with her arms crossed in front

why.why: a woman who is a parent
a woman with her child: a happy picture

radicals.name: 子字旁
radicals.origin: A baby with a big head and little arms wrapped below.
radicals.tip: A big round head on a small body: a child.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means child in 孩 child and 孙 grandchild, but in 学 and 字 it is only part of the shape.

lesson.story: This was a baby with a big round head and arms stretched out, wrapped up below. It means child, and later it became a handy shape in characters about learning and young things.
lesson.picture: a baby with a big round head and wrapped body

why.why: a child under a roof: characters are born from simpler ones
a child under a roof, learning

lesson.shape: It really means child in 孩 and 孙. In 字 and 学 it is mostly just a part of the shape, so do not hunt for a child there.

radicals.name: 口字旁
radicals.origin: An open mouth drawn as a square.
radicals.tip: Just a box for the mouth: whatever happens in it happens around the box.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 口 are usually about the mouth, eating and sounds: 吃 eat, 喝 drink, 叫 call, 唱 sing.

lesson.story: This is simply an open mouth, drawn as a square. Because mouths speak, eat and call out, many characters with 口 are about voices, tasting and eating.
lesson.picture: an open mouth drawn as a small square

radicals.name: 目字旁
radicals.origin: An eye turned on its side, with the pupil in the middle.
radicals.tip: Tip 目 on its side and you see an eye with a pupil.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 目 are usually about eyes and seeing: 看 look, 睡 sleep, 眼 eye.

lesson.story: The old drawing was an eye turned on its side, with the round eyeball in the middle. Later it was stood upright and squared off, but you can still see the eye. It marks looking, seeing and eyes.
lesson.picture: a side view of an eye with a round pupil

why.why: a hand above the eye, shading it
the shiny part of the eye
eyes that close for the night

radicals.name: 耳字旁
radicals.origin: An outline of an ear with its curl.
radicals.tip: The strokes trace the rim of an ear.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 耳 are usually about ears and hearing: 聋 deaf, 聆 listen.

lesson.story: The picture showed an outer ear with its curving rim. Characters with 耳 are about hearing and the ear, though a few words of work and duty use it too.
lesson.picture: a human ear with its curved outer rim

why.why: just a shape here, no ear in the meaning

radicals.name: 提手旁
radicals.origin: A hand with spread fingers, shrunk to three strokes on the left.
radicals.tip: 扌 is a hand reaching out from the left.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 扌 are usually about hand actions: 打 hit, 拿 take, 提 lift, 接 receive.

lesson.story: The full character 手 was a hand with five fingers spread. On the left it is shortened to 扌, with a hook for the arm. It stands for hands doing things: hitting, holding, carrying.
lesson.picture: a hand with five fingers spread out

radicals.name: 竖心旁
radicals.origin: A heart with its chambers; on the left it turns into three upright strokes.
radicals.tip: Three upright strokes: a heart beating on its side.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 忄 are usually about feelings and thinking: 情 feeling, 怕 fear, 懂 understand, 想 think.

lesson.story: The full character 心 was the heart with its chambers. On the left it is squeezed into three short strokes. Characters with it are about feelings and thoughts, which people long felt came from the heart.
lesson.picture: a heart with its chambers and blood vessels

why.why: a happy heart feels light and quick
a heart with no room to rest

radicals.name: 足字旁
radicals.origin: A foot drawn with a square for the ankle and toes below.
radicals.tip: On the left it becomes a small foot standing on the ground.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 足 are usually about feet and foot movement: 跑 run, 跳 jump, 踢 kick.

lesson.story: The top is a round knee or leg and the bottom is a foot. On the left of a character it is pressed into 𧾷. It belongs to walking, running and kicking.
lesson.picture: a lower leg ending in a foot

radicals.name: 页字旁
radicals.origin: Once a person with a big head, now standing for the head and for a page.
radicals.tip: Think of 页 as a head: face and topic live here.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 页 are usually about the head and face: 题 title, 颜 face and colour, 顶 top of head, 领 neck and collar.

lesson.story: The old picture showed a head with a face and a body below it. In writing it moved to mean a page, since a page is like a face turned toward you. Most characters with it are about the head and face.
lesson.picture: a person with a large head and a clear face

why.why: the head of a piece of writing

radicals.name: 月字旁
radicals.origin: Meat on the ribs, squeezed into a moon-like shape when it sits on the left.
radicals.tip: A moon on the left of a body word is flesh, not the moon.
radicals.meaningNote: On the left, 月 is usually flesh and the body: 脸 face, 腿 leg, 脑 brain. In 朋 and 期 it is the moon instead, so watch the position.

lesson.story: This one is tricky. The ancient picture was a piece of flesh or meat, and in words about the body it looks just like the moon 月. So 月 in 脑, 腿 and 脚 is really flesh, not the moon.
lesson.picture: a slice of meat with a crescent shape
lesson.shape: In 有, 朋 and 期 the 月 is the moon or just a shape. Only in body words does it mean flesh.

radicals.name: 舌字旁
radicals.origin: A tongue sticking out of a mouth.
radicals.tip: A tongue poking out of a mouth.
radicals.meaningNote: Mostly a sorting radical. It means tongue in 舌 and 舔 lick, but in 舍 and 舒 the link has faded.

lesson.story: The picture showed a tongue sticking out of a mouth, with a drop of spit flicking off. It is a small shape you meet in words about tasting and speaking.
lesson.picture: a tongue sticking out of an open mouth

why.why: just the shape here, no tongue in the meaning
just the shape here, no tongue in the meaning

lesson.shape: Only in the tongue itself and in 舔 lick does it truly mean tongue. In 舍 and 舒 it is just a shape, so treat it as a handy label.

radicals.name: 身字旁
radicals.origin: A side view of a person with a round belly, as if expecting.
radicals.tip: A big belly and short legs: the whole body.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 身 are usually about the body: 身 body, 躺 lie down, 躲 hide.

lesson.story: This was a side view of a person with a round belly, as if pregnant. It came to mean the whole body. Characters with 身 are about the body and its shape.
lesson.picture: a side-view person with a round belly

why.why: the whole frame of a body

radicals.name: 力字旁
radicals.origin: A flexed arm, or an old plough: power.
radicals.tip: A flexed arm: 力 means strength.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 力 are usually about strength and effort: 动 move, 努 try hard, 助 help.

lesson.story: The old drawing was a strong arm with a muscle, or a plough in the earth. It stands for strength, and many words with it are about effort and work.
lesson.picture: an arm flexed to show a muscle

radicals.name: 三点水
radicals.origin: Three drops of flowing water; the full form 水 shows a stream with splashes.
radicals.tip: Three drops splashing from the left.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 氵 are usually about water and liquids: 湖 lake, 洗 wash, 游 swim, 海 sea.

lesson.story: The full character 水 showed a stream with drops splashing off a flowing line. On the left it shrinks to three drops. If a character has 氵, it is usually about water, liquids, rivers or washing.
lesson.picture: three drops of water splashing from a stream

radicals.name: 火字旁
radicals.origin: Flames licking up from a fire; at the bottom they flatten into four dots 灬.
radicals.tip: Four dots under a character mean heat, like a stove flame.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 火 are usually about fire and heat: 烧 burn, 炒 stir-fry, 灯 lamp, 热 hot.

lesson.story: The picture showed flames leaping up from a fire. At the bottom of a character it often turns into four dots, 灬, like small flames. It is about fire, heat and cooking.
lesson.picture: a fire with three tongues of flame rising

radicals.name: 木字旁
radicals.origin: A tree with branches above and roots below.
radicals.tip: Roots, trunk and branches: three strokes make a tree.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 木 are usually about trees and wood: 树 tree, 林 woods, 桌 table, 椅 chair.

lesson.story: This is a tree with a trunk, branches above and roots below. Characters with 木 are usually trees, wood or things made of wood. Two of them together make 林 woods, three make 森 forest.
lesson.picture: a tree with branches above and roots below

why.why: a tree, with a sound part

radicals.name: 提土旁
radicals.origin: A lump of earth rising from the ground line.
radicals.tip: A mound sitting on the floor line.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 土 are usually about earth and ground: 地 ground, 城 city, 墙 wall, 块 lump.

lesson.story: The old picture was a lump of earth rising from the ground. It stands for soil, land and building ground, so it appears in words about places and walls.
lesson.picture: a mound of earth sitting on the ground

radicals.name: 日字旁
radicals.origin: A round sun, squared off by the brush, with a spot of light inside.
radicals.tip: A window of sunlight: it also means a day.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 日 are usually about the sun, light and time: 明 bright, 晴 clear sky, 早 early, 晚 evening.

lesson.story: The picture was the sun, a round disc with a dot in the middle, later squared off. It stands for the sun and for time and light, so you meet it in days, mornings and bright things.
lesson.picture: the round sun with a dot in the middle

why.why: the sun just above the horizon

radicals.name: 雨字头
radicals.origin: A cloud on top with drops falling beneath it.
radicals.tip: A roof of cloud and four drops: rain.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 雨 are usually about weather: 雪 snow, 雷 thunder, 雾 fog, 露 dew.

lesson.story: The picture was a sky line with drops falling from it. The top bar is the clouds and the dots are the rain. It appears in weather words such as snow, fog and thunder.
lesson.picture: a line of clouds with raindrops falling from it

why.why: a sound from the rain clouds

radicals.name: 石字旁
radicals.origin: A rock 口 lying beneath a cliff edge 厂.
radicals.tip: A rock fallen below the cliff.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 石 are usually about stone and hard things: 破 broken, 碗 bowl, 砖 brick, 码 number.

lesson.story: The old picture was a cliff with a stone lying below it. The top stroke is the cliff edge and the box underneath is the rock. It marks stone, rock and things hard like minerals.
lesson.picture: a rock lying beneath a cliff edge

why.why: stone dug out of the ground

radicals.name: 山字旁
radicals.origin: Three peaks, the tallest in the middle.
radicals.tip: Count the peaks: three, with the biggest in the centre.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 山 are usually about mountains and heights: 山 mountain, 岛 island, 岸 shore, 峰 peak.

lesson.story: This is a mountain with three peaks, the tallest in the middle. It is almost exactly the shape of a real range. Characters with 山 are about mountains, hills and islands.
lesson.picture: a mountain range with three peaks

radicals.name: 田字旁
radicals.origin: A farm field divided into plots by paths.
radicals.tip: It looks like a grid of small plots.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means fields in 田 and 畔 field edge, but in 男 and 界 the field is only a part.

lesson.story: The picture was a square field cut into plots by paths and ditches. It is still a field today. As a shape it mostly appears in words about land and farming.
lesson.picture: a square field divided by paths into plots

why.why: a man works the field with strength
the 田 here is only a shape

lesson.shape: It means field in 田 and 界, and 男 man is a man working in the fields. In 画 and 留 it is just a shape, so do not look for a field there.

radicals.name: 金字旁
radicals.origin: Nuggets of ore buried under a roof: gold, then metal in general.
radicals.tip: 钅 is the squeezed form of 金 on the left.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 钅 are usually about metal and things made of it: 钱 money, 铁 iron, 钟 clock, 针 needle.

lesson.story: The full character 金 means gold or metal and shows lumps in the ground. On the left it shrinks to 钅, with a bar that looks like a tool. It is about metals and things made of metal.
lesson.picture: lumps of metal lying in the ground

radicals.name: 米字旁
radicals.origin: Grains of rice scattered around a stalk.
radicals.tip: A cross with grains in each corner.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 米 are usually about rice and grain foods: 粉 powder, 糖 sugar, 粥 congee.

lesson.story: The picture showed grains of rice scattered on both sides of a line. It means rice and small grains, and so it turns up in words about food made of grain.
lesson.picture: grains of rice scattered around a line

radicals.name: 禾木旁
radicals.origin: A grain stalk with a heavy, drooping head.
radicals.tip: A tree 木 with a bent head of grain on top.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 禾 are usually about crops and harvest: 秋 autumn, 种 seed, 科 branch of study, 租 rent.

lesson.story: The picture was a stalk of grain with heavy ears bending the top over. It means crops and grain, and it also shows up in words about seasons and harvest.
lesson.picture: a plant with a heavy ear of grain bending down

why.why: grain weighed and sorted into kinds
a grain plant grown in water

radicals.name: 两点水
radicals.origin: Two cracks of frozen water, a short version of 冰.
radicals.tip: Two drops, but frozen: just a bit colder than three.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 冫 are usually about cold and ice: 冷 cold, 冰 ice, 凉 cool.

lesson.story: The full character 冰 means ice and shows lines of cracks in frozen water. The two-dot form is a small piece of it. It marks cold, ice and freezing.
lesson.picture: two small ice splinters beside a stream

radicals.name: 夕字旁
radicals.origin: A crescent moon rising in the evening sky.
radicals.tip: Half a moon: it is already evening.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means evening in 夕 and 夜 night, but in 多 and 外 the shape no longer hints at meaning.

lesson.story: The picture was a half moon shining in the evening sky. A crescent moon rises at dusk, so it means evening and night. It is usually a shape in a few common words.
lesson.picture: a crescent moon in the evening sky

why.why: only the shape, no evening here

lesson.shape: It means evening in 夕 and 夜. In 多 and 外 it is just a part of the shape, so treat it as a handy label.

radicals.name: 走之底
radicals.origin: A foot on a road, showing movement along a way.
radicals.tip: The long tail underneath is a road that carries you along.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 辶 are usually about moving along a road: 过 pass, 进 enter, 道 road, 送 send.

lesson.story: The old picture combined a foot and a stretch of road, so it means to walk and travel. It sits low and wraps around the bottom-left of a character like a path. Words with it are about moving, arriving and going far.
lesson.picture: a foot stepping along a stretch of road

radicals.name: 言字旁
radicals.origin: A mouth with words coming out; the left form is just a dot and a flick.
radicals.tip: Speech leaves the mouth from the left.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 讠 are usually about speech and language: 说 say, 请 please, 谢 thank, 读 read aloud.

lesson.story: The full character 言 showed a mouth with words coming out. On the left it is cut down to 讠, a dot and a hook. It marks speech: talking, asking, saying thanks.
lesson.picture: a mouth with words flowing out of it

radicals.name: 立刀旁
radicals.origin: A blade with a cutting edge, standing tall on the right.
radicals.tip: Two upright strokes: a knife ready to cut.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 刂 are usually about cutting: 别 separate, 刻 carve, 剪 cut, 刷 brush.

lesson.story: The full character 刀 was a knife with a handle and a sharp blade. On the right it is pulled into a tall line, 刂. It is about cutting, splitting and sharp things.
lesson.picture: a knife with a handle and a curved blade

why.why: sharp and firm, like a blade

radicals.name: 又字旁
radicals.origin: A right hand drawn in three strokes; it later also meant "again".
radicals.tip: The hand on the right does the job twice: again.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It shows a hand in 友 friend and 取 take, but in 对 and 难 it is only a part.

lesson.story: The picture was a right hand with three fingers. Because a hand can do something over and over, it also came to mean again. It is a hand-shape in many characters.
lesson.picture: a right hand with three fingers extended

why.why: a hand doing it once more
two hands reaching toward each other

lesson.shape: Only in 友 and 双 is it clearly the hand. In many other characters it is just a small shape, so treat it as a label for sorting.

radicals.name: 寸字旁
radicals.origin: A hand with a dot marking the pulse about an inch from the wrist.
radicals.tip: A hand and a small mark: a tiny measure.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It shows a hand in 寸 inch and 导 guide, but in 寺 and 射 the meaning is faded.

lesson.story: The picture was a hand with a small dot marking the pulse spot near the wrist. That distance became an inch, a thumb's width. It is mostly a shape in characters about measuring and hands.
lesson.picture: a hand with a dot marking the wrist

why.why: a hand with a measuring mark
a hand letting go of an arrow

lesson.shape: Only in 寸 and a few characters does it mean hand or measure. In 对 and many others it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 反文旁
radicals.origin: A hand holding a stick to tap or strike something.
radicals.tip: A hand with a stick on the right: teaching, doing.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 攵 are usually about tapping, striking and doing: 教 teach, 数 count, 放 put, 收 collect.

lesson.story: The old picture was a hand holding a stick, ready to tap or strike. It is a shape that stands for doing something with force or purpose. It sits on the right of a character.
lesson.picture: a hand holding a stick about to tap

why.why: guiding with a stick, in the old days

radicals.name: 走字旁
radicals.origin: A person swinging their arms above a foot: walking fast.
radicals.tip: Start moving: 走 holds the person on top and the foot beneath.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 走 are usually about walking and moving fast: 起 get up, 超 surpass, 越 cross, 赶 hurry.

lesson.story: The picture shows a person swinging their arms with a foot below. The top is the swinging body and the bottom is a foot. It means to walk, run and set off.
lesson.picture: a person striding with arms swinging and a foot below

radicals.name: 双人旁
radicals.origin: The left half of 行, a crossroads: a step.
radicals.tip: Two little steps stacked on the left.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 彳 are usually about steps and going: 往 go toward, 径 path, 徒 on foot. In 很 and 得 the link has faded.

lesson.story: This is the left half of a road crossing, a short step. It means a small step on the road. It is found in words about walking, roads and going.
lesson.picture: a small step on the left side of a road

why.why: a step to get what you want

radicals.name: 见字旁
radicals.origin: Once an eye on legs: a person looking.
radicals.tip: An eye 目 with legs: someone seeing things.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 见 are usually about seeing: 见 see, 视 look, 观 watch.

lesson.story: The picture is an eye on top of a walking person: the person is looking. It means to see and to meet. It appears in words about looking and noticing.
lesson.picture: a person with a large eye on top

radicals.name: 欠字旁
radicals.origin: A person opening their mouth wide to yawn.
radicals.tip: Mouth wide open on a person: yawning or breathing.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 欠 are usually about mouth actions like yawning or breathing: 欢 joyful, 歌 song, 吹 blow.

lesson.story: The picture is a person with an open mouth leaning forward, like a yawn. It first meant to yawn or lack something. Most words with it are about the mouth, breathing and feelings that come out.
lesson.picture: a kneeling person with a wide open mouth

why.why: a yawn, a person running short

radicals.name: 止字旁
radicals.origin: A footprint pointing up, meaning foot and then stop.
radicals.tip: A foot that has planted itself: stop.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It shows a foot in 步 step, but in 正 and 此 the meaning has faded.

lesson.story: The picture was a footprint, and it first meant a foot or toe. Later it meant to stop, as when your foot stops. In many characters it is a foot shape, not a stop sign.
lesson.picture: a footprint with toes pointing up

why.why: a foot walking straight to a mark
a foot marching with a spear

lesson.shape: It means a foot in 步 and 正. In many other places it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 戈字旁
radicals.origin: A long-handled weapon with a curved blade.
radicals.tip: A pole with a hook on the right side: a weapon.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It shows weapons in 战 war and 戒 guard against, but in 我 and 成 it is just a component.

lesson.story: The picture was a spear or halberd with a long handle and a blade at the side. It is a weapon shape. It often sits in words about fighting, ruling and contest.
lesson.picture: a spear with a blade on the side
lesson.shape: It is truly a weapon in 戈 and 战. In 我, 成 and 或 it is just a shape, so do not look for a spear there.

radicals.name: 弓字旁
radicals.origin: An archery bow with its string.
radicals.tip: The curved outline of a bow, string drawn.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 弓 are usually about bows and bending: 弯 bent, 弹 shoot, 张 stretch.

lesson.story: The picture was a bow with a string pulled across it. Characters with 弓 are about bows, bending and pulling.
lesson.picture: a curved bow with its string drawn across

radicals.name: 立字旁
radicals.origin: A person standing firmly on a line of ground.
radicals.tip: A person with feet apart on the ground: standing.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means stand in 立 and 站 stand, but in 竟 and 章 it is only part of the shape.

lesson.story: The picture was a person standing on the ground with arms spread, firm on two feet. It means to stand and to set up. It is a shape in words about standing, stopping and building.
lesson.picture: a person standing with arms spread on the ground
lesson.shape: It means stand in 立 and 站. In 亲 and 竖 it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 宝盖头
radicals.origin: The roof of a simple house.
radicals.tip: Like a hat over a little house.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 宀 are usually about houses and shelter: 家 home, 客 guest, 室 room, 安 safe.

lesson.story: The picture was the roof of a house with two sloping sides. Whatever sits under it is indoors. Characters with 宀 are about houses, rooms and being safe inside.
lesson.picture: a house roof with two sloping sides

why.why: a woman under a roof is safe

radicals.name: 广字旁
radicals.origin: A house with a sloping roof and one wall.
radicals.tip: A roof leaning on a wall: a large hall.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 广 are usually about buildings and large spaces: 店 shop, 床 bed, 库 storehouse, 座 seat.

lesson.story: The picture showed a building with a single sloping roof and an open front. It means a large building, a shed or a shop. It sits at the top left of a character and wraps around.
lesson.picture: a large building with one sloping roof

why.why: a piece of furniture in a house
a large building to keep things
only the shape here, no building

radicals.name: 门字框
radicals.origin: Two door leaves swinging on their hinges.
radicals.tip: Look at the frame: two doors with a gap between.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 门 are usually about doors and openings: 问 ask (at the door), 间 room, 闭 close, 闯 rush in.

lesson.story: The picture shows a gateway with two doors swinging open. The two vertical lines are the door posts and the strokes inside are the leaves. It appears in words about doors, gates and openings.
lesson.picture: a gate with two swinging doors

radicals.name: 绞丝旁
radicals.origin: A twist of silk thread tied in loops.
radicals.tip: Twisted threads on the left: silk, cloth, rope.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 纟 are usually about thread, silk and ties: 线 thread, 纸 paper, 绳 rope, 织 weave. In 给 and 红 the link has faded.

lesson.story: The full character 糸 showed twisted threads of silk. On the left it is cut down to 纟. It is about thread, silk and cloth, and also things that join or tie.
lesson.picture: a bundle of twisted silk threads

why.why: silk dyed in a bright colour

radicals.name: 贝字旁
radicals.origin: A cowrie shell, which once served as money.
radicals.tip: Shells were the old coins, so money words wear them.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 贝 are usually about money and trade: 财 wealth, 货 goods, 贵 expensive, 费 cost.

lesson.story: The picture was an open shell. In ancient times shells were used as money, so characters with 贝 are about money, buying, selling and value.
lesson.picture: an open seashell with a ridged shape

why.why: a shell once used as money

radicals.name: 衣字旁
radicals.origin: The collar and sleeves of a robe.
radicals.tip: 衤 is a tunic with a dot for the buttons.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 衤 are usually about clothes and cloth: 衫 shirt, 裤 trousers, 裙 skirt, 被 quilt.

lesson.story: The full character 衣 shows a collar and two sleeves of a jacket. On the left it is shortened with a small hook. It marks clothes and wearing.
lesson.picture: a jacket with a collar and sleeves

radicals.name: 示字旁
radicals.origin: An altar table for offerings to the spirits.
radicals.tip: 礻 is an altar: things to do with worship and luck.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 礻 are usually about worship and luck: 神 god, 祝 wish, 福 blessing, 礼 ritual.

lesson.story: The full character 示 showed an altar table with offerings. On the left it is shortened to 礻. It marks spirits, worship and good fortune, so it is found in words about blessings and rites.
lesson.picture: a stone altar table with offerings

why.why: the way to respect the spirits
a god, honoured at the altar

radicals.name: 食字旁
radicals.origin: A bowl of food with a lid.
radicals.tip: 饣 is a bowl of food on the left.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 饣 are usually about food and eating: 饭 meal, 饿 hungry, 饮 drink, 饱 full.

lesson.story: The full character 食 showed a bowl with a lid on top and food inside. On the left it is cut to 饣. It is about food and eating.
lesson.picture: a covered bowl with food inside

radicals.name: 竹字头
radicals.origin: Two bamboo stalks with leaves hanging down.
radicals.tip: Two leafy tops: bamboo.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with ⺮ are usually about bamboo and things made of it: 笔 pen, 筷 chopsticks, 篮 basket, 算 calculate.

lesson.story: The full character 竹 shows two bamboo stalks with leaves. On top of a character it is shortened to ⺮, called 竹字头. Things made of bamboo, such as pens, boxes and baskets, carry it.
lesson.picture: two bamboo stalks with leaves

why.why: old bamboo strips used for writing

radicals.name: 草字头
radicals.origin: Young sprouts breaking out of the ground.
radicals.tip: Sprouts on a flat line: plants on top.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 艹 are usually about plants: 花 flower, 草 grass, 茶 tea, 菜 vegetable.

lesson.story: The picture was a few blades of grass growing from the ground. On top of a character it becomes two short crossing strokes. It marks plants, flowers, herbs and vegetables.
lesson.picture: blades of grass sprouting from the ground

radicals.name: 车字旁
radicals.origin: A cart seen from above, with wheels at both ends.
radicals.tip: Wheels on an axle, with the body in the middle.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 车 are usually about vehicles and wheels: 轮 wheel, 轻 light, 转 turn, 辆 vehicle.

lesson.story: The picture was a cart seen from above: two wheels, an axle and a body. It was simplified over time but it still means vehicle. It is found in words about carts, cars and wheels.
lesson.picture: a cart seen from above with two wheels

why.why: a vehicle with little to carry

radicals.name: 巾字旁
radicals.origin: A cloth hanging from a belt.
radicals.tip: A towel hanging from a line.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 巾 are usually about cloth and fabric: 帽 hat, 布 cloth, 带 belt, 席 mat.

lesson.story: The picture was a piece of cloth hanging from a belt or a pole. It means cloth, scarf or towel. It is found in words about cloth, hats and flags.
lesson.picture: a square cloth hanging down

radicals.name: 尸字头
radicals.origin: A body lying down; later it also looks like a roof over a space.
radicals.tip: Imagine a person sitting under a low roof.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It shows a body or building in 尺 and 屋 room, but in 局 and 层 the link is faded.

lesson.story: The old picture was a person lying down or sitting with bent legs, and it came to mean a body. In characters today it is mostly a roof-like shape. It is a sorting label, not something you read as a body.
lesson.picture: a person seen sitting or lying, side-on
lesson.shape: In 屋, 局 and 层 it works like a roof, not a body. Treat it as a sorting label.

radicals.name: 耳刀旁
radicals.origin: On the left it is a hill with steps; on the right it is a walled town.
radicals.tip: Left means hills, right means towns.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. On the left it hints at hills (阳 sunny side, 陪 accompany), on the right at towns (都 capital, 邮 post), but many characters have no such link.

lesson.story: This one has two lives. On the left it is a mound of earth, like stairs or a hill. On the right it is a city, a settlement. On the left it is about slopes and heights, on the right about places.
lesson.picture: a hill with steps on the left, a town on the right

why.why: a walled space, like a hill

lesson.shape: On the left it is a hill, on the right it is a city. Check the side to know which one is meant.

radicals.name: 王字旁
radicals.origin: Three pieces of jade strung on a cord.
radicals.tip: Same as 王 the king, but it is a string of jade beads.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means jade in 玉 and 琴 zither, but in 现 球 理 the jade meaning has faded.

lesson.story: The full character 玉 was a string of jade beads. 王 here is the jade shape with the dot dropped. It stands for jade and jewels and is found in names of gems and round things.
lesson.picture: jade beads on a string

why.why: the gleam of polished jade appears

lesson.shape: It is about jade in 球 and 珠. In 王 king and 班 it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 皿字底
radicals.origin: A shallow dish with a foot.
radicals.tip: A bowl on a stand: the base of the character.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 皿 are usually about dishes and containers: 盘 plate, 盒 box, 盆 basin.

lesson.story: The picture was a dish or bowl on a base. It means a container for food. Characters with it are about bowls, plates and things you serve.
lesson.picture: a bowl on a short stand

radicals.name: 国字框
radicals.origin: A walled boundary around something.
radicals.tip: A fence that holds another character in.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It is an enclosure in 国 country, 园 garden and 圆 round, but in 因 and 回 it is only the box shape.

lesson.story: This is a square wall around something. Whatever is inside is enclosed. It marks places and limits: countries, gardens, circles.
lesson.picture: a square wall around an open space

why.why: a space with a wall around it

lesson.shape: It is a boundary in 国, 园 and 圈. In 四 and 因 it is just a box, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 厂字头
radicals.origin: A cliff overhang that makes a sheltered spot.
radicals.tip: A cliff that covers the character beneath it.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It is a cliff in 厂 and 厦 building, but in 原 and 历 the link is faded.

lesson.story: The picture was a cliff with a hollow beneath it, like a shed against a hill. It is a shape in words about slopes, sheds and factories.
lesson.picture: a cliff with a shelter underneath

why.why: a shed at the foot of a hill

lesson.shape: It is a cliff shelter in 厂 and 厚. In 历 and 压 it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 酉字旁
radicals.origin: A jar for brewing wine.
radicals.tip: A jar with a belly full of wine.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 酉 are usually about wine and fermenting: 酒 liquor, 醉 drunk, 酸 sour.

lesson.story: The picture was a tall jar for wine with a neck and a belly. It means wine and drink. In ancient times it also marked making and storing alcohol.
lesson.picture: a tall wine jar with a narrow neck

why.why: a sour taste from a jar

radicals.name: 舟字旁
radicals.origin: A little boat with its ribs and hull.
radicals.tip: Lines for the planks: a small boat.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 舟 are usually about boats: 船 boat, 航 sail, 舰 warship.

lesson.story: The picture was a small boat with a deck and planks. It means boat and ship. You will find it in words about boats and sailing.
lesson.picture: a small boat with planks and a deck

radicals.name: 户字头
radicals.origin: A single-leaf door, half of a pair of gates.
radicals.tip: Half a door: one family.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means door in 户 and 扇 fan-leaf, but in 房 and 所 the link has faded.

lesson.story: The picture was a single door leaf, one half of a double door. It means door and household. It sits over words about rooms, houses and openings.
lesson.picture: a single door leaf swinging on its hinge

why.why: a flap like a door leaf

lesson.shape: It means door in 户, 房 and 扇. In 所 it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 穴宝盖
radicals.origin: A cave with a rough roof over its mouth.
radicals.tip: A cave with a lid on top.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 穴 are usually about caves and hollows: 空 empty, 窗 window, 穷 poor.

lesson.story: The picture was a cave in a hillside: a roof with two dots for the opening. It means cave and hole. Characters with it are about openings, hollows and digging.
lesson.picture: a cave opening in the side of a hill

why.why: a dog jumping out of a hole

radicals.name: 反犬旁
radicals.origin: A dog seen from the side, tail up, shrunk on the left.
radicals.tip: The curl on the left is an animal ready to pounce.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 犭 are usually about animals: 狗 dog, 猫 cat, 猪 pig, 狼 wolf.

lesson.story: The full character 犬 was a dog with a curled tail, seen from the side. On the left it is squeezed into 犭. It appears in words for dogs and wild animals, and for some animal-like behaviour.
lesson.picture: a dog standing with a curled tail

why.why: a dog, with a sound part

radicals.name: 马字旁
radicals.origin: A horse with a mane and four legs.
radicals.tip: Still has a mane at the top and tail curling away.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 马 are usually about horses: 骑 ride, 驾 drive, 驶 steer.

lesson.story: The picture was a horse with a mane, four legs and a tail, turned on its side. Over time it became a few strokes, but you can still see the head, mane and body. It marks horses and riding.
lesson.picture: a horse with a flowing mane and four legs

radicals.name: 鸟字旁
radicals.origin: A bird with a beak, a body and a tail.
radicals.tip: The dot is the eye of the bird.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 鸟 are usually about birds: 鸡 chicken, 鸭 duck, 鹅 goose.

lesson.story: The picture was a bird with a beak, an eye, wings and feet, seen from the side. It marks birds and bird-like creatures. Over time the feet became four dots in the full form.
lesson.picture: a bird with a beak, an eye and a tail

radicals.name: 鱼字旁
radicals.origin: A fish with head, body and tail.
radicals.tip: The bottom line is the tail fin.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 鱼 are usually about fish: 鲜 fresh, 鲸 whale, 鲨 shark.

lesson.story: The picture was a fish with a head, a scaly body and a tail. In the modern form the tail became four dots. It is found in words for fish and things from the water.
lesson.picture: a fish with a head, scales and a tail

why.why: a fresh fish, a sweet taste

radicals.name: 虫字旁
radicals.origin: A crawling worm or snake.
radicals.tip: A worm with a head and curl: bugs and critters.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 虫 are usually about insects and small creatures: 蚊 mosquito, 蜜 honey, 蜂 bee, 蛇 snake.

lesson.story: The picture was a snake or a worm coiled up, with a head at the top. In Chinese it covers insects, worms and small crawling things, not only bugs.
lesson.picture: a coiled worm or small snake

radicals.name: 羊字旁
radicals.origin: A sheep seen from the front with its curved horns.
radicals.tip: Horns on top and a body: a sheep.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means sheep in 羊 and 羔 lamb, but in 美 and 群 it is only a component.

lesson.story: The picture was a sheep seen from the front: two curved horns, a face and a body. It stands for sheep and goats, and also for something gentle and good.
lesson.picture: a sheep seen from the front with curved horns

why.why: a big, plump sheep to eat

lesson.shape: It really means sheep in 羊 and 群. In 美, 鲜 and 养 it is a hint of something good, not an animal, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 牛字旁
radicals.origin: The head of an ox with horns.
radicals.tip: A horned head with a line down the middle.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means cattle in 牛 and 牧 herd, but in 物 and 特 the link has faded.

lesson.story: The picture was an ox seen from the front: a head with two horns pointing up. It means ox and cow. As a sorting shape it appears in a few common words.
lesson.picture: an ox head with two horns pointing up

why.why: cattle were a main item of wealth

lesson.shape: It really means cattle in 牛, 牲 and 牧. In 物 and 特 it is only a sorting label for the meaning, so do not look for an ox.

radicals.name: 病字旁
radicals.origin: A person lying on a bed.
radicals.tip: A sick person leaning on a bed.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 疒 are usually about sickness and pain: 病 ill, 疼 ache, 痛 pain, 瘦 thin.

lesson.story: The picture was a person lying on a bed, with a sign of being unwell. It means illness. Words with it are about sickness, pain and the body feeling wrong.
lesson.picture: a person lying on a sickbed

radicals.name: 白字旁
radicals.origin: A ray of white light or a thumb tip.
radicals.tip: A sun with a ray on top: white.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means white in 白, but in 的 and 百 it is only a component.

lesson.story: The picture was a thumb or a sun ray, and it came to mean white and clear. Today it is mostly a shape, though it still means white in the character itself.
lesson.picture: a white thumb or a ray of light
lesson.shape: Only 白 itself means white. In 百, 的 and 皇 it is just a shape, so treat it as a sorting label.

radicals.name: 大字头
radicals.origin: A person stretching their arms and legs wide.
radicals.tip: A person with arms wide: big!
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means big or a person in 大 and 天 sky, but in 夫 and 夹 it is only a component.

lesson.story: The picture was a person with arms and legs spread wide, to show how big he is. It means big. As a shape it appears in many characters where something is large or a person stands out.
lesson.picture: a person standing with arms and legs wide apart

why.why: a person with arms stretched wide
the big thing above a person
a grown man with a hairpin

lesson.shape: It really means big in 大 and 太. In 头 and 奇 it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 隹字旁
radicals.origin: A small bird with a short tail, seen from the side.
radicals.tip: A bird perched on a line, with feathers drawn as strokes.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 隹 are usually about birds: 集 gather, 雄 male, 雀 sparrow.

lesson.story: The picture was a short-tailed bird, small and round. It is a shape in words for birds, especially small birds, and for gathering, as birds gather in a tree.
lesson.picture: a small bird with a short tail

radicals.name: 羽字旁
radicals.origin: Two wings with feathers.
radicals.tip: Two feathers side by side.
radicals.meaningNote: Characters with 羽 are usually about feathers and flight: 翅 wing, 翻 flip, 翼 wing.

lesson.story: The picture was two feathers side by side. It means feather and wing. Characters with it are about flying, wings and soft things.
lesson.picture: two feathers side by side

radicals.name: 小字头
radicals.origin: Three tiny dots for small bits.
radicals.tip: Three little specks: small.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means small in 小 and 尖 pointed, but in 少 it is only a component.

lesson.story: The picture was three small dots or specks, to show something tiny. It means small. In many characters it is a shape that stands for fine or little.
lesson.picture: three tiny specks, one in the middle

why.why: small at the top, big below

lesson.shape: It really means small in 小, 少 and 尖. In 当 and 常 it is only a shape on top, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 十字旁
radicals.origin: A cross: counting all ten on both hands.
radicals.tip: A cross: ten.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means ten in 十 and 千 thousand, but in 午 noon and 南 south it only gives the shape.

lesson.story: The old drawing was a simple cross, a way to count all ten fingers of both hands. It means ten. As a shape it appears in numbers and in a few other words.
lesson.picture: a plain cross made of two crossing strokes
lesson.shape: It is a number in 十 and 千. In 午 and 南 it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 横
radicals.origin: One horizontal line.
radicals.tip: One stroke: one.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means one in 一 and 三 three, but in 不 and 世 it is only a stroke.

lesson.story: The picture was one line lying flat. It means one and also stands for a flat surface. In many characters it is only a stroke, not a number.
lesson.picture: one flat horizontal line
lesson.shape: It is a number in 一 and 三. In 不, 世 and 万 it is just a stroke, so do not look for a number there.

radicals.name: 儿字底
radicals.origin: A person with two legs, often at the foot of a character.
radicals.tip: Two legs at the bottom: a person walking.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It shows a person with legs in 儿 child and 兄 elder brother, but in 先 and 光 it is only the bottom shape.

lesson.story: The picture was a person with two legs, and these days it often sits at the foot of a character. On its own it also means child or son. Most of the time it is just the legs of a character.
lesson.picture: a person standing on two legs

why.why: a foot ahead of a person

lesson.shape: It means child in 儿 and 兄. In 先 and 光 it is just the legs at the bottom, so treat it as a label.

radicals.name: 八字头
radicals.origin: Two lines pulling apart, to divide.
radicals.tip: Two strokes parting like a door opening.
radicals.meaningNote: Mainly a sorting radical. It means eight in 八, but in 公 and 六 it is only a component.

lesson.story: The picture was two lines parting, as if something were being split in two. It means eight, and also divide. In characters it often marks something splitting or spreading.
lesson.picture: two strokes bending apart
lesson.shape: It means eight in 八 and 六. In 公 and 共 it is just a shape, so treat it as a label.
